_doc: PROOF scenario for the owner rule "subtitles are never burned into the picture by default" on the SILENT (captions-only) path. A demo_video whose brief sets `captions_only: true` and whose deliverable OMITS `captions_mode` (so it stores the default `none`). compile_stage.captions_mode() promotes `none` + captions_only to `overlay`, so the compiler must MUX a soft mov_text track (+ the captions.srt sidecar) and never burn text into the pixels. demo_video_narrate skips TTS on this path (narrate.py captions_only branch), so there is no narration clip to assert on. Authored `lines` (same TodoMVC target as demo_video_relief) keep the bdd generation path out of the bill; three ~15-20-word lines at the 3 words/s reading pace (shared/captions_only.py) give a ~20-25s film against the 25s order. The `expect_subtitles` gate reads: burned (derived captions_render from config_snapshot, the only retrievable source — the compile request itself is not persisted), soft_track (ffprobe subtitle streams of the DELIVERED master, delivered_artifact_url), srt_min_cues (GET /api/runs/{id}/captions.srt). Every one of them FAILS when unobserved, never defaults green.
